parties: <cite index="1-1">Sunshine Pictures Limited, a fresh issue of 48,00,034 equity shares and offer for sale of 30,37,157 equity shares</cite>
headline: <cite index="1-1,1-4">Sunshine Pictures Limited launched a ₹282.14 crore IPO; Vidhigya Associates served as sole legal counsel</cite>
sum: Entertainment production house Sunshine Pictures raised ₹282.14 crore via a mainboard IPO comprising a fresh issue of 48,00,034 equity shares and offer for sale of 30,37,157 equity shares. The stock listed on NSE and BSE on 25 August 2026, with shares listing at ₹395.90 on NSE, a 9.97% premium to the ₹360 issue price.
implication: The 105.81x oversubscription in a mid-market entertainment IPO signals strong institutional and retail investor appetite for content-production assets with IP monetisation rights-a structuring precedent for media-and-entertainment issuers leveraging hybrid production models (co-production + solo IP ownership) to de-risk content cash flows.
detail: <cite index="1-6,1-7">Sunshine Pictures is an entertainment content production company engaged in originating, developing, producing, marketing and distributing feature films, television serials, web series and other audio visual content, having produced 13 commercial films (including self-produced and co-produced films), two web series, three television serials and one short commercial film</cite>. <cite index="2-4,2-11">The company planned to utilise ₹112.50 crore from its ₹172.80 crore net fresh issue proceeds towards working capital requirements, with the remaining amount earmarked for general corporate purposes</cite>. <cite index="3-2">The IPO opened on August 18 and closed on August 20, 2026, with the issue priced at ₹360 per share</cite>. <cite index="2-6,2-8">The IPO received bids for 58,04,90,382 shares against 54,86,051 shares available for subscription, with non-institutional investors leading demand with a subscription of 197.04 times and qualified institutional buyers subscribing 123.52 times their allocated portion</cite>.

framework.note: Central regulation governing book-built IPO process, price-band setting, subscription mechanics and allotment.
Governs dematerialisation, crediting of allotted shares, and demat account linkages for IPO allottees.
Core provisions for issuing prospectus, public offer mechanics, and statutory filing with RoC.
Post-listing compliance, disclosure obligations, and corporate governance requirements on both BSE and NSE.
Film content regulation; relevant for Sunshine Pictures' production of feature films requiring CBFC certification.
Governs IP creation and rights monetisation from films, web series, music and ancillary content.
Relevant to digital content distribution, OTT and streaming rights; cybersecurity compliance for content platforms.
GST treatment of entertainment services, production fees, and content distribution revenue.
Post-listing insider trading rules for promoters, directors, officers and substantial shareholders.

structure.novel: Hybrid production model combining co-production (risk-shared with studios for fixed fees) and standalone IP-ownership (theatrical, OTT, music rights monetisation); first mainboard IPO for a Bollywood independent production house with focus on commercial films rather than studio integration.

triggers.note: Book-built IPO mechanics, anchor allocation, price-band finalization and public subscription.
Film production and CBFC certification requirements for all theatrical releases.
IP creation and monetisation of multiple content rights (theatrical, OTT, music, ancillary).
Post-listing governance, continuous disclosure, and related-party transaction approvals.
